newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No damaging cold in sight for Brazil coffee--Somar.
newsitem.headline: No damaging cold in sight for Brazil coffee--Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions face no risk of damaging cold in the next five days, with any polar air masses all passing through the far south of the country, local meteorologist Somar said Thursday.

Minimum temperatures in the last 24 hours ranged between eight and 12 degrees Celsius, with the lowest temperatures in Pocos de Caldas, traditionally Brazil's coldest coffee area in highland southern Minas Gerais state.
Minimum temperatures in the coming days should remain between eight and 15 degrees Celsius, with no rains forecast, Somar said.
The current forecast extends to July 29.
On that date, a high pressure system is forecast in the Pacific Ocean with an intensity of 1,024 millibars, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
The high pressure system would only pass through Brazil at the beginning of August and so as yet it was too early to say if if it would affect the coffee regions.
"This is the only one. After that, there should be nothing else (which would affect coffee)," Massari said.
